FINAL HYPOTHESIS (natural language):

"Amber, measured as its Z-score of social capital, attained its highest value (Z = 1.54) in the **4th millennium BCE**, peaking in the interval **~3300–3000 BCE (≈ 5250–4950 calBP, −3300 to −3000 CE)**. The maximum of 1.54 forms a sustained 4-century plateau across the bins 3300, 3200, 3100, 3000 BCE in both the raw time-series (`Amber`) and capital (`Zamber`, comma-decimal parsed) series, which are identical (max |difference| = 0 on all 37 overlapping century bins); the yearly interpolated series holds 1.54 constant over that 301-year window. Strictly, the plateau's value persists through 3000 BCE — the nominal first year of the 3rd millennium BCE — so of the 301 peak-years, 300 (99.7%) lie in the 4th millennium BCE (4000–3001 BCE) and only the single boundary year 3000 BCE falls in the 3rd millennium BCE; the peak itself unambiguously belongs to the 4th millennium BCE (single-max-year reading: 3300 BCE). The peak is robust to smoothing: rolling means of 50–200 yr all keep their maximum (1.54) inside this window."

WORKFLOW:
1. Parsed `Zamber` from comma-decimal strings in capital.csv; confirmed the BCE axis (4300→500, 100-yr steps, no gaps) and the CE/calBP axes of time_series_data.csv (1-yr steps, CE −4100→+500, calBP = 1950 − CE).
2. Verified the amber series is consistent across files: `Amber` (raw century bins) and `Zamber` are identical on all 37 overlapping bins (max |Δ| = 0); `Amber_inter` is the yearly linear interpolation of those bins (301 fully non-null years).
3. Identified the global max Z = 1.54 in all three views (raw, capital, interpolated).
4. Defined the peak interval as the sustained full-max-elevation window: bins 3300/3200/3100/3000 BCE in both raw series; CE −3300…−3000 (calBP 5250…4950, 301 years) in the interpolated series.
5. Confirmed robustness with 50/100/150/200-year rolling means (argmax always inside the plateau, value 1.54).
6. Assigned the millennium in BCE convention: peak year 3300 BCE and 300/301 (99.7%) of plateau years lie in the 4th millennium BCE (4000–3001 BCE); the single boundary year 3000 BCE is the nominal first year of the 3rd millennium BCE, stated explicitly. pollen dataset excluded (no amber column, verified).

Key diagnostics: raw max 1.54 at BCE 3300 (and 3200/3100/3000); Zamber max 1.54 at BCE 3300; Amber_inter constant 1.54 CE −3300..−3000 (301 yr); rolling-mean argmax CE −3275/−3250/−3225/−3200 for windows 50/100/150/200; peak-year reading 3300 BCE → 4th millennium BCE. All assertions passed.
